This model mapped our inputs directly to our outputs

followed by a softmax operation.

evidence_contexts.source_text: One of the key features of a bidirectional RNN is that information from both ends of the sequence is used to estimate the output.

As a specific example
illustrated in :numref:`fig_nlp-map-sa-rnn`,
we will represent each token
using the pretrained GloVe model,
and feed these token representations
into a multilayer bidirectional RNN
to obtain the text sequence representation,
which will
be transformed into 
sentiment analysis outputs :cite:`Maas.Daly.Pham.ea.2011`.
:numref:`fig_birnn` illustrates the architecture of a bidirectional RNN with a single hidden layer.
Bidirectional RNNs were introduced by :cite:`Schuster.Paliwal.1997`.
Hence, if we were to use a bidirectional RNN naively we would not get a very good accuracy: during training we have past and future data to estimate the present.
*Bidirectional RNNs* add a hidden layer that passes information in a backward direction to more flexibly process such information.

In deep bidirectional RNNs with multiple hidden layers,
such information
is passed on as *input* to the next bidirectional layer.

![Architecture of a bidirectional RNN.](../img/birnn.svg)
:label:`fig_birnn`
Synthetic: A bidirectional RNN reads the sequence in both directions, unlike a unidirectional RNN.

proposed_definition_en: a recurrent neural network architecture that processes a sequence in both forward and backward directions
